title: FORGE: Self-Evolving Agent Memory With No Weight Updates via Population Broadcast
overlap_reasoning: Covers three of our four elements in weakened form. (a) Social transmission: yes, horizontal champion broadcast every stage; provenance is trivially known (the champion is logged in incremental_summary.md) but is not tracked per-excerpt. (b) Capability as a variable: yes, four model families compared and the headline qualitative finding 'weaker base models gain most / capability gap narrows' is already published, which directly pre-empts one of our intended results. (c) Readable trace: yes, memory is plain YAML text diffs snapshotted before/after each stage (definitions_initial vs definitions). (d) Heritable memory practice: no. The practice (rules vs examples vs mixed, max 100 rules / 50 examples, reflection trigger threshold) is a fixed experimental condition in the config, not something agents edit or inherit; only memory content evolves. Adversarial caveat: structurally FORGE's loop (copy champion to all, each instance then diverges through independent reflection, select best) is a (1,lambda)-style evolution strategy, i.e. inheritance with variation in all but name, so a reviewer may say 'inheritance with variation' is not new; our distinguishing claim must rest on the policy file being the heritable object and on economic selection. Evidence that would settle residual doubt: the full paper's discussion of whether the Rules/Examples/Mixed choice is ever adapted online (README says no), and whether any cost-aware selection was tried.
what_we_can_borrow: Use FORGE as the nearest baseline and as the capability-gap citation we must position against. Borrow: (1) the champion-broadcast vs isolated-Reflexion ablation design as our 'horizontal transmission on/off' control; (2) the graduation/freeze idea as a cheap compute saver and as a contrast to our death rule; (3) their YAML snapshot-per-stage layout (definitions_initial vs definitions) as a model for our per-night markdown diffs; (4) the Rules-vs-Examples representation comparison, which maps onto what our agents' policy files may converge to; (5) their token-usage logs per instance as a precedent for reporting cost even without an economy. Also cite their reported 'Rules cost ~40% fewer tokens' as motivation for why an economy should select toward rule-like memory.
